chunks.arabic_text: عَنِ ابْنِ الْمُتَوَكِّلِ، عَنِ الْحِمْيَرِيِّ، عَنِ ابْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ، عَن أَبِي وَلَادٍ، عَن أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ قَالَ

translations.en: From Ibn al-Mutawakkil, from al-Himyari, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abi Wallad, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

chunks.arabic_text: كَانَ عَلِيُّ بْنُ الْحُسَيْنِ عَلَيْهِمَا السَّلَامُ يَقُولُ: إِنَّ الْمَعْرِفَةَ بِكَمَالِ دِينِ الْمُسْلِمِ تَرْكُهُ الْكَلامَ فِيمَا لَا يَعْنِيهِ، وَقِلَّةُ الْمِرَاءِ، وَحِلْمُهُ، وَصَبْرُهُ، وَحُسْنُ خُلُقِهِ

translations.en: Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) used to say: The recognition of the perfection of a Muslim's religion [is seen in] his avoiding speech in what does not concern him, his sparing of argumentation, his forbearance, his patience, and his good character.

en.summary: Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) defines the perfection of a Muslim's religion through five ethical traits: avoiding irrelevant speech, minimizing arguments, exercising forbearance, practicing patience, and maintaining good character.
en.seo_question: What are the signs of a Muslim's religious perfection according to Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn?
